EVE Online is a sandbox MMORPG set in a persistent sci‑fi universe, where you can pilot ships, mine resources, manufacture goods, explore, engage in massive PvP battles, or dive into intricate politics and economics. It’s one of the most ambitious MMO experiences ever made. (store.steampowered.com
)

Strengths:
✔️ Immense freedom: You can choose any career — trader, pirate, miner, explorer, fleet commander — and carve your own path.
✔️ Epic scale battles: Some fights involve thousands of players, creating staggering, cinematic space warfare.
✔️ Deep economy and politics: Player-driven markets and alliances give the universe a living, breathing feel.
✔️ Constant updates: CCP consistently adds ships, mechanics, and events, keeping veteran and new players engaged.
✔️ Unique community: Long-term players create stories, alliances, betrayals, and events that are legendary in gaming.

Weaknesses:
✖️ Steep learning curve: New players can feel completely lost for weeks, which can be intimidating.
✖️ Time-intensive: Progression often requires patience — ships, skills, and influence take time to build.
✖️ Harsh PvP: Losing a ship can be devastating; “learning by dying” is brutally real.
✖️ Pay-to-speed temptation: Omega subscription speeds up skill training and access to ships, which can feel mandatory for serious players.
✖️ Complex UI: The interface is dense and can overwhelm newcomers trying to navigate ships, markets, and fleets.

Overall impression:
EVE Online is deep, rewarding, and one of the most unique MMOs ever created, but it demands patience, persistence, and a willingness to learn. Its stories and massive battles are unlike anything else in gaming.

It's not for everyone — the learning curve is very steep, time investment can be massive, and the game rewards patience, planning, and social connections. But if you enjoy true freedom, high-stakes decisions, and being part of living player history.

citations.review_text: This game is incredibly unintuitive to play.  If you do not have a community of people to help you with "how the game functions" then you will spend DAYS doing mundane tasks, or screaming at your computer because you have no idea what to do next.  The tutorial missions are vague, instructions on how to even move around in space are nonexistent.  Its an old game, and if you didn't start 15 years ago, skip it.

[h1] Lost in Space Without a Purpose  [/h1]

The trailer looks exciting—like Crossout or World of Tanks, but in space. But instead of actually playing, you just keep clicking "Next" to sit through dialogue between two AIs.

You’re thrown into space without a tutorial or any explanation; the basic controls aren't explained, nor is the game's objective. I have no idea what the game wants me to do. It tells you to "warp" somewhere without explaining how to use the warp function. You get sent to locations without knowing why.

There is simply a total lack of explanation or any sense of connection to the game. Essentially, you just drift aimlessly through space and get frustrated by the non-existent controls after clicking through another 20 minutes of dialogue.

No thanks—I’d rather have something with action, or at least a clear purpose and goal.

EVE Online is not just a game about spaceships. It is a living universe where every alliance, betrayal, trade deal, and battle creates its own story.

The scale of EVE is almost impossible to describe. You can become a miner, trader, explorer, pirate, industrialist, mercenary, or fleet commander. The game gives you freedom, but it also expects you to learn and survive in a universe where other players can be just as dangerous as any NPC. 🌌

The economy is one of the most impressive parts. Almost everything is created and controlled by players, from basic equipment to massive warships. Markets, corporations, and alliances create a level of depth that few games can match. 💰⚔️

Large-scale battles are legendary, and the social side of the game is where EVE truly shines. Joining a corporation and working toward a shared goal can create some of the most memorable gaming moments you will ever experience. 🤝🚀

The learning curve is brutal. The interface can be overwhelming, progress can feel slow, and losing expensive ships because of one mistake is painful. This is not a game that explains everything—it expects you to adapt.

I started as a rookie flying a tiny ship. I ended up reading spreadsheets, negotiating deals, and preparing for battles that lasted hours. Somehow... I loved it. 😂

EVE Online: where losing a spaceship hurts, but the story of how you lost it becomes legendary. 🌠

This game is SO good. You'll never ever see anything like this in another game. It's a total open world sandbox where every action you take as a player shapes this world. some people call it job sim or spreadsheet simulator, but that's only one part of the game. You can just go around blowing ♥♥♥♥ up if you want. You can fight pirates and rogue AI and robots, not just other players. A lot of people think that eve is either a spreadsheet sim or a sweaty PvP no life game, but that simply isn't true. New eden has a place for anyone and everyone. I've also heard people complain that this game is toxic and difficult for new players to learn. There are COUNTLESS youtube videos and such for anything and everything in this game. And if you still have questions, and are looking for an active and friendly community, Look for the EVE University corporation in game. they're entire thing is teaching new and returning players the ropes and are some of the most friendly people you'll meet in new eden. Eve isn't for everyone, and new players are definitely fighting a bit of an uphill battle, but to me that's what makes this game so fun. I get to find ways to do things that I "shouldn't" be able to do, or that other players can do better, and say screw it, imma do it anyway. While scams for new players are true, Eve's entire atmosphere is that unless RMT is involved, it's legal. You treat it like you treat real life: If something seems too good to be true, 9/10 times it is. claims.claim: Reviewers note that core progression elements, such as higher-level ships, modules, and advanced skill training, are restricted behind the monthly Omega subscription model.

citations.review_text:
I wish I could recommend this game. It is one of the most beautiful and in-depth games ever made. Unfortunately, it is not "free to play." Sure the first 100 to 200 hours are but once you get hooked and start loving every aspect of the game, you realize you need to pay for a monthly subscription to play the game fully. You can't fly certain ships, can't use certain modules, can't research certain skills, and the list goes on. Core game mechanics that let you progress and make an impact are locked behind a $20 a month subscription.

I can recommend this game to those that are willing to give their all into it. Those that have been looking for this game for years and are willing to drop every other game (and maybe hobby) to play EVE Online. I think the game is worth it if you are in that category.

I was going to write wall of text on what I dislike about EVE and how to fix it, but in the end - devs never listen to their community and pursue their own abstract goals.
So I ended up with few most pressing points / showstoppers (imho of course):
[list]
[*] Ganking. And no real way to defend from it.
[*] No skill training past skill-points threshold for 'alphas'. Lose omega == lose 99% of game entertainment, ships you've earned and equipment you've got.
[*] Forced PvP you can't avoid.
[*] Grind in the name of the grind. Wrost thing is that here grind won't even make you feel more powerful, its just pointless repetition of mindless activities day-by-day.
[list]

So after 10-15 year hiatus, I decided to try to get my account back up and see how things have changed.  

Within a week this is what the game and it's community provided:
1.)  My old character was unplayable because all of the things I earned before the Plex system are now under the omega pass restriction. 
      *  No higher level weapons, ships, or upgrades
2.)  I created a new character to go through they new player friendly tutorial.
      *  The rewards were nice but with people actively ganking, you will loss everything quickly
      *  The combat mission system was overly dangerous in the beginning with absolute junk payouts.
      *  The mining missions paid well but I lost two ships within three days.  If it wasn't for the previous 
          Plex I had the character would have been stuck in a cruiser.
3.)  When talking with others about experiencing the ganking being almost constant, I was told well you have to be on your toes at all times.
4.)  I will not pay a monthly fee to be fed upon by others.  The game rewards bad behaviors.  The people that kill your stuff are also the people you buy replacements from.  Because they make sure you can mine what you need to build your own.

The TLDR of it:  If you like games like Rust, where most players goals is to steal or destroy your stuff, then EVE is for you.  If you are looking for a CO-OP game, this isn't it.

This is why their player base is so low.  And I know the fanboys will say cry more.  I say, not my money or time ever again.
